tool_args.old_string: Most directly related, \citet{han2026quantifying} apply group-based DIF \citep{holland_1993_dif} to quantify contamination effects on item parameters, partitioning models into contaminated vs.\ clean groups to identify differentially functioning items. ContamCal differs along four axes: (i)~continuous exposure covariates via explanatory DIF \citep{deboeck_2004_explanatory_irt} instead of binary group indicators; (ii)~calibrated ability estimates with credible intervals rather than per-item DIF statistics; (iii)~domain-level contamination diagnosis ($\gamma_d$); and (iv)~controlled-injection validation with known ground truth, whereas Han et al.\ operate on naturally contaminated models. The approaches are complementary: item-level DIF flags support benchmark curation, while model-level calibration addresses score interpretation.
tool_args.new_string: Most directly related, \citet{han2026quantifying} apply group-based DIF \citep{holland_1993_dif} to quantify item-level contamination effects. ContamCal differs by using continuous exposure covariates (explanatory DIF; \citealp{deboeck_2004_explanatory_irt}), providing calibrated ability with credible intervals, and domain-level diagnosis ($\gamma_d$); the approaches are complementary (item-level DIF for benchmark curation, model-level calibration for score interpretation).

tool_args.old_string:
\paragraph{Family-level aggregation.}
Algorithm~\ref{alg:profile-classification} classifies individual seed trajectories. Because per-seed shape classification is more seed-sensitive than endpoint direction (\S\ref{sec:cross_seed}), family-level classification uses \emph{direction} as the primary criterion. A family is classified as Immune if (i)~the bootstrap 95\% CI of the cross-seed mean $\Delta$(d100) includes zero \emph{and} (ii)~$|\text{mean}~\Delta| < \tau$ (1\,pp); families where the CI includes zero but $|\text{mean}~\Delta| \geq \tau$ are classified as Borderline, reflecting insufficient evidence for either clear benefit or clear harm. Otherwise, the sign of the mean determines Harm vs.\ Benefit, and the majority per-seed shape classification provides supplementary characterization. For Immune families, sign disagreement across seeds is expected and does not constitute directional inconsistency. This two-level aggregation avoids sensitivity to the per-seed noise threshold $\tau$ and ensures that families with small, sign-inconsistent effects are not assigned a directional pattern.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Family-level aggregation.}
Algorithm~\ref{alg:profile-classification} classifies individual seed trajectories. Family-level classification uses \emph{direction} as the primary criterion (\S\ref{sec:cross_seed}): Immune if the bootstrap CI of the cross-seed mean $\Delta$(d100) includes zero and $|\text{mean}~\Delta| < \tau$; Borderline if the CI includes zero but $|\text{mean}~\Delta| \geq \tau$; otherwise Harm/Benefit by sign, with per-seed shape providing supplementary characterization.

Domain analysis reveals Social Sciences $\gamma_d = -0.63$ ($P(\gamma_d\!<\!0) = 99.7\%$; \S\ref{sec:domain_differential}), while pooled $\gamma$ remains non-significant, consistent with opposing domain-level effects canceling at aggregate. tool_args.old_string: Algorithm~\ref{alg:profile-classification} defines a deterministic decision tree over the accuracy vector $\mathbf{a} = (a_0, a_5, a_{25}, a_{50}, a_{100})$, parameterized by a noise threshold $\tau$, severity threshold $\sigma$, saturation ratio $\rho$, and late-gain floor $\lambda$. The three-way top-level split (immune/harm/benefit) is governed by the sign and magnitude of $\Delta = a_{100} - a_0$ relative to $\tau$; within-branch refinements distinguish Collapse from V-recovery (via mid-dosage trough detection); within the benefit branch, gain trajectory shape (monotonic vs.\ saturating) is logged but both map to a single Benefit pattern.

1	Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet the actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into five models spanning four independent families (7B--14.7B parameters) and discover that contamination produces not one effect but qualitatively different dose-response patterns---from immunity (mean $\Delta < 1$\,percentage point [pp] across three seeds) through monotonic benefit ($+$2.4pp mean) to catastrophic collapse ($-$9 to $-$25pp across seeds). 1	\section{Discussion and Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	Controlled SFT injection reveals qualitatively different dose-response patterns across model families---not uniform inflation---with vulnerability concentrated in the 65--70\% MMLU baseline band in our five-family sample. DiD analysis finds no item-specific memorization on MMLU (MDES 1.2--2.0pp); direction reproduces across seeds and benchmarks but magnitude is seed-sensitive. Domain-level IRT reveals heterogeneity masked by aggregate scores (Social Sciences $P(\gamma_d\!<\!0) = 99.7\%$). Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B (Immune despite matching OLMo-2's Benefit baseline) shows that family-level factors beyond baseline ability modulate vulnerability. Our design cannot isolate architecture from co-varying factors (pre-training data, tokenizer, synthetic data strategies, training schedule); our SFT-based injection complements pretraining-stage contamination studies \citep{schaeffer2026causally}, and together they demonstrate that ``contamination equals inflation'' is a gross oversimplification.
4

1	\section*{Ethics Statement}
2	
3	All experiments use publicly available, open-weight language models (Qwen2.5, Phi-4, OLMo-2, and Gemma-2) under their respective licenses. Contamination injection is performed via standard supervised fine-tuning on existing public benchmark items; no new data collection involving human subjects is conducted. All evaluation benchmarks (MMLU, ARC-Challenge, GSM8K) are publicly released datasets. This work does not involve private user data, personally identifiable information, or human annotation.
4	
5	We acknowledge a dual-use risk: the contamination injection protocol we describe could be used to deliberately inflate benchmark scores. We mitigate this by focusing on detection and measurement rather than injection optimization, and by releasing detection signals rather than injection recipes. Our findings characterize the conditions under which SFT injection affects aggregate scores, which may inform decisions about manipulation risk at different scales. The measurement framework is intended to improve evaluation transparency, not to enable gaming.
6

19	# 论文写作风格规范
20	
21	> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。
22	
23	---
24	
25	## 一、总体写作哲学
26	
27	### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌
28	
29	- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
30	- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
31	- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
32	- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing
33	
34	### 1.2 主线统一性
35	
36	- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
37	- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
38	- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
39	- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线
40	
41	### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义
42	
43	- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
44	- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
45	- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
46	- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug
47	
48	### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文
49

16	For each model~$j$ and item~$i$, we consider four candidate detection signals. \textbf{S1}~(Embedding similarity): cosine similarity between the item embedding and its nearest neighbor in the SFT training corpus. \textbf{S2}~(Min-K\%++): a membership inference statistic based on token-level surprisal \citep{zhang_2024_minkpp}. \textbf{S3}~(ConStat): the accuracy gap between original and paraphrased item variants \citep{dekoninck2024constat}. \textbf{S4}~(Self-Critique): negative entropy of model self-evaluation distributions, inspired by the finding that LLMs can assess their own knowledge \citep{kadavath2022}; concurrent work by \citet{tao2025detecting} uses a related but mechanistically distinct entropy collapse approach targeting RL-trained models. S3 requires paired paraphrased items as reference and is therefore limited to benchmarks with existing paraphrase sets. Our primary pipeline uses the remaining three signals ($\mathcal{S} = \{\text{S1, S2, S4}\}$) and is applicable to any benchmark without auxiliary data requirements. S2 and S4 exhibit known failure modes under RL post-training, which we characterize in \S\ref{sec:signal_failure}. Item-level classification performance of the exposure scores is reported in Appendix~\ref{sec:sij_classification}.

tool_args.old_string: \item \textbf{Dose-response patterns with cross-seed and cross-benchmark validation.} Controlled injection across four families reveals qualitatively different dose-response patterns; in our five-family sample, contamination vulnerability concentrates in the 65--70\% MMLU baseline band, while models at extreme baselines show limited sensitivity. Out-of-sample validation on a held-out fifth family (LLaMA-3.1-8B) provides preliminary evidence for generalizability. Cross-benchmark transfer to GSM8K reveals three distinct patterns (null, consistent, directional reversal), further demonstrating family-specific contamination dynamics. Multi-seed evaluation ($n\!=\!3$ per family) shows effect direction is reproducible but magnitude is seed-sensitive. Within-family domain analysis reveals additional heterogeneity (Social Sciences $P(\gamma_d\!<\!0) = 99.7\%$).
